text: The absolute daily-dollar condition applies to organizations and projects, triggers on the last daily billed amount exceeding a configured USD threshold, and excludes credits applied for the previous day from that billed-amount calculation. Do not assume this documented credit treatment also applies to percentage-change conditions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The monthly current-bill condition for any single project applies at organization scope and uses a threshold for all projects; it resets when the pending invoice closes. Its scope differs from the project-only percentage-change conditions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

OneUptime’s March 31, 2026 tutorial posts PENDING_INVOICE_OVER_THRESHOLD to a project alertConfigs endpoint. This example conflicts with the official condition documentation, which limits monthly current-bill conditions to organizations; treat the snippet as unverified rather than as a working project billing-change configuration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-31)

Atlas exposes daily, weekly, and monthly project billing percentage-increase conditions. Configure these from Project Alerts; their alertable event names are DAILY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD, WEEKLY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD, and MONTHLY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The alertable project event identifiers are DAILY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD, WEEKLY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD, and MONTHLY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD. Their corresponding *_BILLING_CHANGE_NORMAL events are listed as non-alertable. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A historical feature request asked for per-project billing alerts in May 2020; a reply on May 11, 2020 directed users to project-scoped alert settings. The request title and submitted status alone therefore do not establish that project-level billing alerting is absent. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2020-05-11)

DoiT advertises Atlas project- and cluster-level cost views, budgets, and cost-anomaly alerts. These are DoiT integration capabilities and do not establish the calculation or delivery semantics of native Atlas project billing-change events. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

A MongoDB billing design case study reports that interviewed users wanted to monitor multiple projects without repeatedly checking individual bills. It describes contextual alert setup prompts as a design proposal, so it does not prove that the proposed interface shipped. (low confidence)

Project billing-change events are distinct from ORG_DAILY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD, ORG_WEEKLY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD, and ORG_MONTHLY_BILLING_CHANGE_OVER_THRESHOLD. Organization gross-spend conditions explicitly compare the previous day, previous 7 days, and previous 30 days; the project condition descriptions do not specify those same comparison formulas. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Managing project alerts requires Project Owner or Project Alerts Manager access. Organization Owners must add themselves to the project as Project Owner to manage its alerts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The send-if-condition-lasts and resend-after controls are available only for Host alerts; Atlas explicitly excludes billing and other event-based alerts from these controls. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
